chapter: Working with Duke and final reflections
title: Bee Ellington and being turned away from Duke
summary: Whaley recalls Bee, a former chorus girl, whom Duke treated as a wife, and says she would not let him wake Duke before the hospital.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Because Ruth was never -- you know, Evie was sickly, see.
Oh, Bee. She was a chorus girl at the Cotton Club.
Sure, she was a chorus girl ...
Oh yeah, I worked with Bee.
Yeah, and she ended up at the Cotton Club in New York on Broadway and 48th Street. Bee was the lady's name.
Wait a second. Okay, so you were saying Duke took Bee and did what?
Well, she afforded him a great deal of happiness in his lifetime.

Oh yeah, she was great to me. I went down to see Duke when I was blind, and she was -- this was just before Duke was taken to the hospital, and Duke was asleep and she wouldn't let me wake him up. She made me go out of the house.
And he did marry her before he died, right?
That's what he said -- he married her.
He didn't tell me that he married her, but he told somebody else that he married her.
Because they only let me up at the hospital once up there at the Columbia Center, the Columbia Presbyterian. I went up there only once.
